## Structure Requirements

| Need | Evidence-based response |
|---|---|
| Buildable product areas | Foundation/access, community, classroom/session content, calendar, search, administration/moderation, security/operations, content readiness, quality/launch. |
| Traceability | Every work package and backlog item links to one or more approved RQ IDs or an explicit operational deliverable. |
| Hidden work | Include deployment, HTTPS, backups, restore testing, monitoring, moderation rules, content loading, participant testing, and final acceptance. |
| Conditional work | RQ-17 video protection and RQ-18 SSO remain conditional until decisions are made. |
| Deferred work | RQ-19 exclusions remain outside the backlog and protected from accidental re-entry. |
| Sequencing | Build a vertical slice across access, content, playback, and files before broad feature completion. |
| Ownership | Use `TBD` where the project has not assigned an owner; do not infer individual ownership. |

PM-13 can produce a formal product-backlog structure for the approved Option B baseline. The structure must expose conditional decisions, hidden operational work, and unassigned owners. It must not reuse the WordPress backlog as the new baseline or add deferred capabilities.
